overall: The AG found the Boston Zoning Board of Appeals violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide requested open session minutes within ten days; it ordered only immediate and future compliance, noting prior training and warning that future violations may be treated as intentional.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to provide requested open session minutes of two 2014 meetings within the 10-day period required by the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Indeed, the Board failed to provide the requested minutes until it responded to the Open Meeting Law complaint more than five weeks later.

allegations.summary: Board argued the request was not received by the current executive secretary; the AG found that did not excuse the 10-day response obligation.
allegations.key_passage: While Mr. Small may no longer have been a Board employee at the time the request was received, that did not absolve the Board of its obligation to respond to a request for open session meeting minutes within ten days.

allegations.summary: Not in the original complaint, the AG noted the minutes of the two 2014 meetings were handwritten, hard to read, and lacked enough detail for the public.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the minutes are inadequate to inform the public as to what the Board discussed during its September 2 and 23, 2014 meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant also requested a Board decision along with the minutes; the AG declined to review that request because it is a public records matter, not an Open Meeting Law matter.
allegations.key_passage: Our review concerns only compliance with the Open Meeting Law, thus we decline to review the allegation as it pertains to documents other than minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no training ordered; the Board had already attended an OML training on November 15, 2016).
remedy_passage: Because the Board participated in this training, and because the events addressed in this letter took place prior to the training, we order only the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
